text: I looked up Aqua Crest on the NSF certification site and was not able to find their refrigerator filter certification. I then looked up EveryDrop (Whirlpool brand) and could find their certifications. Next I checked out the AquaCrestFilter.com website. It is basic and whois reveals that it is registered through a Alibaba probably for a Chinese company. There is no ownership information on the AquaCrest website. Per website they claim NSF 42 (chlorine and particulate class 1) and NSF 372 (Components are lead free). The filter is not certified to filter out lead or other heavy metals; that's NSF 53. Everydrop's filter 6 is NSF 53 certified and you can find the details on the NSF certificate on their website, not so for AquaCrest.

Bought this filter to try as a replacement to the Whirlpool/Pur 4396701 filters I had been using for 15 years without issue in our Kenmore top freezer fridge with internal water dispenser.  Reading some of the reviews and questions, I was concerned there may be a fitment issue.  I installed it today and ran 2 quarts of water through it without any issues.  This filter is a little different in that the end nearest where you install it is a smaller diameter versus the Whirlpool filter.  The end by the inlet is the same size so this filter is tapered versus constant diameter for the Pur/Whirlpool filter.  The cap still fit on the end fine though and the filter installed easily without leaks.  The locking feature on the filter appears different but in my case it did not affect the installation.

I'm not a coffee drinker so I don't know what makes a coffee filter "good", but these seem sturdy and do their job well. I used some store brand filters to strain homemade yogurt and they always tore when I would scoop the yogurt off of them. So I tried these Melitta Natural Brown ones and I'm glad I did! They're a bit thicker than typical white filters, which made me skeptical at first, but it really seemed that they strained out more whey in a faster time. Plus, I've only had 1 tear out of maybe 20 that I've used do far. I definitely plan to repurchase these when I run out.
